summary: The page header bar. Renders Figma's Desktop, Tablet, Mobile-Closed and Mobile-Open from one DOM tree.
useWhen: the app needs a top bar with a brand, navigation and actions
that bar must collapse to a mobile menu below 896px

useInstead.when: it is a sidebar rather than a top bar
useInstead.why: Header owns a horizontal bar and its own breakpoint behaviour

brand.note: rendered at the start; never shrinks

center.note: inline on Desktop and Tablet; moves into the mobile menu below 896px. Rendered once, so slot state survives crossing the breakpoint

children.note: escape hatch — rendered in the bar after the menu wrapper and before the mobile toggle. Prefer the named slots

a11y.role: banner, from the <header> element when it is a direct child of body
guarantees: the mobile toggle carries `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the menu container
Escape closes the open mobile menu — and the listener sits on the header, so a header that never opens never listens
the slots are rendered once, so no nav link exists twice in the accessibility tree
requires: `menuLabel` — the mobile toggle is icon-only and has no other name
notes: This is a disclosure, not a modal: no focus trap and no scroll lock, so Escape is the whole dismissal contract.

antiPatterns.dont: rendering a second copy of the nav for mobile
antiPatterns.why: Header already moves the one copy; two copies duplicate every link in the accessibility tree

antiPatterns.dont: driving the mobile layout from JS state
antiPatterns.why: the breakpoint is a media query — the browser already knows the answer, and duplicating that judgement is how the two drift
controlled with no handler means the toggle can never change it
